Alex — great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the 2-week POC we discussed. Please reply with confirmations/edits.

Call recap
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for FinLytics' document-to-structured extraction pipeline (mapping & normalization) in production-like traffic.
- Primary success criteria: >=85% mapping accuracy on your evaluation set; hallucination rate <5% (measured on the 5k test set); acceptable cost per 1k tokens (TBD).
- Timeline: kickoff week of Mar 9 -> 2-week trial -> evaluation dashboard + recommendation.

Workload / traffic intake (we need confirmation / more detail from you)
- Steady-state RPS: ?
- Typical concurrency: ?
- Peak burst behavior (RPS & duration): ?
- Prompt length (tokens avg): ?; expected response tokens (avg / p95): ?
- P95 latency SLO target (ms): ?

Proposed POC plan (high level)
1) Week 0 (pre-kickoff): finalize scope, provide us sample data + evaluation labels, set up staging keys.
2) Week 1: ingest sample workload, run integration + scale tests, collect metrics.
3) Week 2: run evaluation suite (5k golden examples), iterate on model/quantization/config, deliver dashboard and recommendation.

Ownership
- Marissa (me): POC owner & customer success lead — overall timeline, eval criteria, and success decision.
- Ben Carter (cc): Solutions engineer — environment setup, load tests, performance tuning.
- Vivek Kulkarni (cc): Account exec — commercial / SLA coordination.

Attachments: FinLytics-POC-runbook.xlsx (skeleton) and trial-SLA-draft.pdf (terms draft).

Next steps (please):
- Confirm: steady RPS, typical/peak concurrency, avg prompt/response token lengths, latency SLO.
- Reply with preferred kickoff dates the week of Mar 9.

Subject: Re: POC planning — FinLytics / Redwood trial next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear plan. Confirming the workload details below, and a couple of clarifications on the success criteria so we align.

Workload profile (production-like staging traffic)
- Steady-state RPS: ~15 requests/sec (most of our traffic is worker-based ingestion).
- Typical concurrency: 8–12 concurrent requests.
- Peak bursts: up to ~120 RPS sustained for 2–3 minutes, happening roughly every 45–90 minutes during peak ingestion windows.
- Prompt tokens: avg 120 tokens (mostly short docs and a structured prompt template).
- Response tokens: avg 450 tokens; p95 ~950 tokens for long documents.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms desirable; we can tolerate up to 500ms during peak bursts for the POC.

Evaluation plan & success criteria
- We'll provide a 5k labeled test set (mapping + normalized outputs). Primary metric: mapping accuracy (target >=85%).
- Secondary: end-to-end correctness spot checks for normalization; hallucination rate target <5% (we'll annotate a 500-sample audit).
- Cost target: we're tracking $/1k tokens vs current vendor; ballpark target under $1.20/1k tokens for inference (open to Redwood recommendations).

Kickoff availability: week of Mar 9 — Mar 9 or Mar 10 morning PT preferred.

Files: I'll upload the 5k sample + evaluation labels to the shared Drive link after you confirm where to put them (staging or private S3).

Thanks — Alex
Alex Harper
Head of ML Engineering, FinLytics
alex.harper@finlytics.com

Perfect — thanks for the details, Alex. Everything looks achievable. Confirming the kickoff: Mar 9 at 9:30am PT (I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm).

Immediate actions (owners):
1) Marissa (me): finalize runbook and upload staging instructions + one-time staging API key.
2) Ben: prepare a Redwood sandbox (dedicated tenant) with expected concurrency headroom and an initial load test profile matching the burst pattern (15 RPS steady, bursts to 120 RPS for 3 minutes). Estimate required GPU resources and suggested model variant/quantization to meet the 300ms p95 target.
3) Vivek: prepare trial commercial terms + ensure the trial-SLA-draft.pdf covers the timeline and data handling.

Ben — for load testing, can you provide an initial config within 48 hours? Helpful specifics: batch sizes, KV cache warm-up strategy, and expected tokens/sec per GPU at the suggested model/quantization. That will let us scope Dedicated vs Hosted for the trial.

Alex — please share the 5k labeled set via the Drive link in the HubSpot record or let me know if you prefer S3 (we have short-lived ingestion credentials for staging).

I'll attach an updated runbook after Ben's initial sizing. Looking forward to kickoff.

Best,
Marissa

Ben / Vivek — forwarding the thread from Alex (FinLytics). Key asks for our side:

- Ben: please provision a dedicated sandbox for FinLytics with the following starting config:
  * Model variant: redwood-large-1 (quantized int8 recommended)
  * Initial batch size: 8–16 (tune based on latency), continuous batching enabled
  * KV cache warm-up: pre-warm by replaying 500 requests before peak windows
  * Target p95 latency: <= 300ms at steady-state; allow up to 500ms during bursts
  * Load profile: steady 15 RPS, bursts to 120 RPS for ~3 mins every ~60 mins
  * Token assumptions: prompt avg 120, response avg 450, p95 950

- Provide a rough GPU estimate + expected tokens/sec per GPU and a short note on whether Dedicated or Hosted sandbox makes sense for the POC cost-wise.
- Build the initial load test script and run a smoke test before the Mar 9 kickoff.

Vivek: please queue the trial-SLA-draft with legal and prepare an initial allowance (credits + short-term pricing) so we can sign off quickly after the kickoff if the trial looks good.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/FinLytics | https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/abc123
